newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks tread water, close rangebound.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks tread water, close rangebound.

text.p: Argentine stocks mimicked Wednesday's action and closed virtually flat in slack volume Thursday, marking time ahead of the U.S. presidential elections, dealers said.

"The market is entirely moving on short positions by speculators. All the big investors have pulled out and are waiting to see what happens Tuesday in the United States," said Jorge Bonanno at Interfin traders.
The blue-chip MerVal index .MERV closed at 570.34, unchanged since last Tuesday, while the broad market index edged up 0.2 percent.
Technical analysts said the MerVal faced resistance at 570-575 and lacked the necessary volume to push any higher.

But analysts noted the fresh rally in U.S. Treasuries Thursday was a good omen for the markets. "It seems to anticipate tomorrow's all-important jobs figure, which if tame should further alleviate any inflationary fears ahead of the November 13 Federal Reserve meeting," said another trader.

The U.S. long bond yield continued its week-long slide Thursday, ending at 6.64 against a 6.83 close Monday. "People snatched their profits when the yield first tumbled Tuesday and they're holding their bets now," said Bonanno.
Bolsa floor volume slowed to 12.5 million pesos from 13.5 million Wednesday, while over-the-counter deals eased to 69.5 million pesos against 64.6 million Wednesday.
Risers beat losers 26 to 18 and 23 issues closed flat.
Strongest main-tier gainers were construction stock Juan Minetti and holding company comercial del Plata, both up 1.7 percent, and Telecom, which tacked on 1.2 percent.
MerVal losers were headed by Banco de Galicia and Banco Frances, which shed 3.4 percent and 2.8 percent, respectively, on profit-taking after recent bond-driven gains, dealers said.
